This handbook is here to guide both international and local members of our community—students
and faculty alike—through the essentials of joining Mapúa’s global programs. Whether you are
arriving from abroad to study or teach, or you are a local member preparing to take part in an
exchange or international collaboration, this resource is designed to help you navigate university
policies, academic expectations, and the many support services available.
It offers practical tips for adapting to campus life, succeeding in your studies, and making the
most of international opportunities. You’ll also find guidance on mobility processes, from visas
and enrollment for inbound participants to program requirements and preparation for outbound
exchanges.
Because Mapúa University continuously enhances its programs and aligns with both national and
international standards, updates may occur. For the latest information, please check official
announcements or reach out to the International Office.
If you have questions or need assistance, the Office of International Linkages, Relations, and
Development Cooperation (ILRAD) is ready to support you. Contact us at ilrad@mapua.edu.ph or
call +63 (2) 8 2475000.
We encourage all students and faculty—whether inbound or outbound—to read this handbook
carefully and follow the guidelines for a smooth and enriching experience.
ABOUT THIS HANDBOOK
 Office of International Linkages, Relations, and Development Cooperation © 2026. All Rights Reserved.

Dear Students and Faculty,
Welcome to Mapúa University! Whether you are joining us from across the globe or are
part of our local community eager to explore international programs, we are thrilled to
have you with us. 
Choosing Mapúa means joining a community that values inclusivity, collaboration, and
cultural exchange. We believe that learning goes beyond classrooms—it’s about building
friendships, sharing experiences, and discovering new ways of seeing the world.
To help you settle in and make the most of your journey, we’ve prepared this International
Handbook. Inside, you’ll find practical guidance on university policies, campus life, and
resources to support both your academic success and personal growth. For international
students, it also includes helpful information on visas, enrollment, and adjusting to life in
the Philippines. For our local community, it offers insights into international programs and
opportunities to connect globally.
All times mentioned in this handbook follow Philippine Standard Time (UTC+8).
We look forward to seeing you thrive, explore, and create lasting memories at Mapúa
University. Welcome to your new adventure!

PREPARATION BEFORE
COMING TO THE PHILIPPINES
WHAT TO PACK
We recommend carrying cash, credit cards, and a discreet money belt for security. Be
sure to bring:
1.Airline ticket/s for your flight/s to the Philippines.
2.Prescription medications you need, along with written prescriptions from your
doctor.
3.Passport, valid for at least six months.
4.Student visa and permit documents (see 1.2 IMPORTANT DOCUMENTS).
5.University admission letter and proof of financial support (see 1.2 IMPORTANT
DOCUMENTS).
6.One complete change of clothing and toiletries, in case your checked luggage is
delayed.
7.Driver’s license and an international driving permit, if you plan to drive.
8.Emergency contact information and copies of important documents (keep digital
backups).
9.Rain gear (umbrella or raincoat) and light clothing, suitable for tropical weather.

OFF-CAMPUS LIVING
Plan Early
Expect rent near universities to range from ₱5,000–₱15,000 per month. Include
utilities, internet, and transportation in your budget.
There is no on-campus housing in Mapúa University. Arrange your off-campus
accommodation before arrival. You can check the list of off-campus accomodation
using this link: https://www.mapua.edu.ph/pages/admissions/faqs.
Verify Remotely
Request a copy of the lease and the landlord’s ID. Schedule a video tour and never
pay full rent upfront.
Watch for Red Flags
Avoid properties without written agreements or receipts. Be cautious of very low
rent prices or pressure to pay before arrival.

WHAT TO DO: ACR I-CARD, STUDY VISA AND PERMIT
Foreign nationals intending to study at Mapúa University must first be admitted to an academic
program and hold a valid visa, usually a 9(F) Student Visa. The 9(F) visa may be obtained before
arrival through a Philippine Embassy or Consulate, or after arrival through visa conversion,
subject to approval by the Bureau of Immigration.
Tourist visa and dependents 21 years old and above under working or investor visas (such as
9G, SIRV, 47(a)(2), and similar visa types) are required to convert to a 9(F) Student Visa to
continue studying. Dependents of diplomatic visa (9E) holders and SRRV holders are exempt
from this requirement, provided the principal’s visa status remains valid; otherwise, conversion
to a 9(F) visa is required.

Are foreign students allowed to work
in the Philippines?
Foreign students in the Philippines cannot work for pay on
a regular student visa. 
Working without permission can lead to fines, deportation,
or visa cancellation.
Can foreign students drive or rent a
car in the Philippines?
Yes. Foreign students can drive with a valid International
Driving Permit (IDP) and their home country license, or a
Philippine driver’s license if staying long-term. They can
rent a car if they meet the rental company’s requirements,
usually including passport, valid license, and minimum
age.
Can foreign students travel abroad
while studying in the Philippines?
Yes, but they must have a valid student visa and re-entry
permit (if required). They should also ensure their
passport is valid and check entry requirements of the
destination country.
For dual passport holders, they will use their Philippine
passport when leaving the country.
For naturally-born Filipinos but are naturalized citizens of
foreign countries, an active Philippine passport or ACR i-
CARD is required.
